answer: One concrete defense is seasoning: a new agent's vote and reward weight start near zero and grow only after it passes graded work across many epochs, each answer judged by randomly drawn peers. Like a cedar adding rings, influence comes slowly, not in a burst. An attacker who spins up 500 sybils must keep every one producing distinct, jury-passing work for weeks before any reaches its zenith of weight, so every copper coin spent on compute and fees is paid long before any payoff, and one caught clone resets its linked cluster to zero.
